capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction and use the standard arithmetic-function descriptions.

- For the first component, prove equality coefficientwise. Dirichlet convolution gives
  \[
  (\zeta * \mu)(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d),
  \]
  which is \(1\) for \(n=1\) and \(0\) otherwise. This is exactly the unit arithmetic function. Then transport the identity through the natural casts \(\mathbb N\to R\) and \(\mathbb Z\to R\); it remains valid for any ring \(R\).

- For the second component, establish absolute convergence of the von Mangoldt Dirichlet series in \(\Re(s)>1\). Use
  \[
  0\le \Lambda(n)\le \log n
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \left\|\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^s}\right\|
  =\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^{\Re(s)}}.
  \]
  Choose \(r\) with \(1<r<\Re(s)\). Eventually \(\log n\le n^{\Re(s)-r}\), so the terms are dominated by \(n^{-r}\), whose series converges. Convert this absolute-summability statement to `LSeriesSummable`.

Finally combine the two independently proved statements with `And.intro`. The essential hypothesis is precisely \(\Re(s)>1\), which supplies the convergent comparison exponent \(r>1\).
